## Owner Duplicate Detection — Findings

The project is Spring PetClinic REST converted to OfficeFloor function injection. Duplicate detection is currently **three independent, separate checks** (telephone, email, household) wired as sequential steps in the `POST /api/owners` pipeline — there is **no** consolidated `identityKey`. ### 1. Build file & running tests
- **Build file:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml` (Maven). Parent: `spring-boot-starter-parent` 4.1.0; OfficeFloor 4.0.2 via `net.officefloor.springboot:officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter`. - **DTO generation:** `OwnerFieldsDto` (package `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto`) is **generated at build time** by `openapi-generator-maven-plugin` 7.23.0 from `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — there is no hand-written source file for it. Fields include `firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone, email, registrationDate, sharesHousehold` (request-only opt-in).
- **Run tests:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/mvnw test` (or `./mvnw verify`). Wrapper scripts `mvnw`/`mvnw.cmd` at repo root.

### 2. POST owners pipeline
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml` — guarded by `authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"`. - **`EnsureUniqueTelephone.java`** — compares the already-E.164-normalized telephone via `ownerRepository.findByTelephone(request.getTelephone())`; throws `DuplicateTelephoneException` if any match. Runs *after* `NormalizeOwnerTelephone` so comparison is E.164-based.

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java` declares the lookup methods used by the checks: `findByTelephone(String)` (exact match on normalized value), `findByEmail(String)` (case-insensitive, lower-cased input), `findByLastName(String)`. - `DuplicateTelephoneException.java` — msg `"Telephone is already in use: …"`
- `DuplicateEmailException.java` — msg `"Email is already in use: …"`
- `DuplicateHouseholdException.java` — msg `"An owner with the same last name and address already exists: …"`

- `DuplicateEmailExceptionHandler.java` → `["email"]`
- `DuplicateHouseholdExceptionHandler.java` → `["household"]`

- `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.DuplicateTelephoneException.yml`
- `…DuplicateEmailException.yml`
- `…DuplicateHouseholdException.yml`
(each is a one-step `handle:` mapping to its handler class.)

### 8. Tests
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` — the only duplicate-specific test: `coreRejectsIdentityCollision()` creates an owner, then a second owner reusing the first's `telephone`, and asserts **409 Conflict**. - `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — black-box base (`@SpringBootTest @AutoConfigureMockMvc @Transactional @WithMockUser` admin). Note it references features not all wired yet (postcode, structured address, Idempotency-Key).

No other duplicate/conflict tests exist in the test tree.

    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepted in national or international form
            (spaces, dashes and brackets are ignored); stored and returned in E.164 form,
            assuming country code +61 when none is supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional; defaults to the server's current date when not supplied.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Request-only opt-in acknowledging that this owner deliberately shares a household with an
            existing owner. When true, the create endpoint skips the duplicate-household rejection that
            fires when another owner already has the same last name and address.
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of the first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality: the canonical region derived from the city using the fixed
                city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN'
                when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>', where CITY3 is the upper-cased
                first three letters of the city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three letters of the last name,
                and NNNN a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence number (one more than the owners already in

The change is complete and the build passes. Here's what I did.

## Summary

I consolidated the three separate duplicate checks (telephone, email, household) on `POST /api/owners` into a single derived **identity key**, and now expose that key on the owner response.

**The identity key** — `<normalizedTelephone>|<email or empty>|<householdId or empty>` — lives in one place, as a derived `@Transient` getter on the `Owner` entity (`Owner.getIdentityKey()`), alongside the existing derived getters (`getLocality`, `getContactPreference`, `getInitials`). This is the single source of truth used both for the check and for the response.

**The single check** — new `EnsureUniqueIdentity` function replaces `EnsureUniqueTelephone`, `EnsureUniqueEmail`, and `EnsureUniqueHousehold`. It compares the new owner's whole identity key against existing owners and rejects (409) only on an exact full-key match. Since telephone is the first key component, an existing owner can only collide if it shares the telephone, so it reuses the existing `findByTelephone` lookup as the candidate set rather than scanning everything.

**Ordering** — the check runs *after* `AssignHousehold` (so the new owner carries its final `householdId`, part of the key) and *before* `SaveOwner`, under the same `transaction` governance, so a collision rolls back before anything persists. `NormalizeOwnerTelephone`/`NormalizeOwnerEmail` still run first, so the key is built from normalized values.

**Behaviour change (per spec):** two members of the same household (same `householdId`) with different telephones now have different keys and are both allowed — only an exact full-key match is a duplicate.

**Return** — added a read-only `identityKey` to the `Owner` schema in `openapi.yml`; MapStruct maps it onto `OwnerDto` automatically by name.

**Cleanup** — deleted the three obsolete check functions, the three `Duplicate*Exception` classes + handlers, and their escalation YAMLs; added `DuplicateIdentityException` + handler (409, body `{"errors":["identityKey"]}`) and its escalation YAML; updated the `Household` javadoc that referenced the removed class.

Test result: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — `AcceptanceTest.coreRejectsIdentityCollision` passes, **BUILD SUCCESS**.
